prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "poetry", with the standing line "A desktop notebook where literary definitions, written with inline tags, weave themselves into a searchable, self-checking web of words, writers and titles." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows One large open entry card holds a paragraph of definition prose with three highlighted inline tags. From each tag a thread runs outward to a separate smaller entry card. The first thread goes to a Reference, the second to a Writer, the third to a Title. Arrows point from tag to target. Threads leaving the big card are marked outgoing links. A few threads arriving from other cards are marked incoming links. Every card rests on a single database cylinder below.

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows the search index looking up words across all cards at once, with boolean joiners. The second shows a tag being typed that points to a missing card, and a ghost card offered for quick-create. The third shows a speaker beside a Writer card for pronunciation. The five small studies show a tag with no thread, a card with no threads at all, two cards bearing the same name, a card with an empty definition, and a tag of an unrecognised kind. The final group shows the database leaving as a structured file, a readable document and a stack of dated backup copies.

Colour is used so that Ochre marks a tag that has become a link. Muted red marks a flaw a report has caught.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 3 tag kinds, one count mark on each tag in ; 5 report checks, counted across ; 2 export formats, marked in ; 7-day rotation of daily backups, drawn as seven stacked copies; 500-entry graph limit, noted in .

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: {w:} on the tag threading to the Reference card, {p:} on the tag threading to the Writer card, {t:} on the tag threading to the Title card, poetry.db on the database cylinder, FTS5 on the search-index circle, quick-create on the ghost card, Unlinked References, Orphaned Items, Duplicate Items, Missing Definitions and Unknown Tags on their studies, JSON Export and Markdown Export on the outgoing files, Daily Backups on the stacked copies.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: poetry.db, definition, {w:}, {p:}, {t:}, Reference, Writer, Title, outgoing links, incoming links; FTS5, AND OR NOT, regex mode, quick-create, pronunciation; Unlinked References, Orphaned Items, Duplicate Items, Missing Definitions, Unknown Tags; JSON Export, Markdown Export, Daily Backups, 7-day rotation; write, parse, link, search, graph, export

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Tags in the prose become links; Deleting an entry removes its links. The search index updates on every change; Missing targets offered as new entries. Reports catch tags and links that disagree; Orphans have no connections at all. Markdown export turns tags into names. The graph shows up to 500 entries.
